About & methods

Built by Jonno Millar to turn the numbers behind the points into captain, transfer and chip decisions. Explore the published squad, compare mini-league results, or use Scout to find and compare players.

Player statistics come from the public Fantasy Premier League API, including Opta's expected goals and expected assists. Their sum, expected goal involvement (xGI), describes the quality of chances a player takes and creates. Fixtures, market odds and predicted line-ups inform the analysis.

Projections are estimates. Advice uses the last published squad and bank, so check your actual team before acting. Double-gameweek planning is unsupported. Snapshots refresh on a best-effort schedule; their age and any unavailable sources are shown below.

Starting XI

Season and Last gameweek use your last published team. Next gameweek selects the best legal XI from your owned squad, then lets you preview the recommended transfers. Player xP is before captain or chip multipliers. Pitch xP uses match histories; the transfer plan uses its season-based scorer. Projected team totals include captain/chip multipliers and any transfer hit. C is captain, V is vice-captain, and IN marks an incoming transfer. CS is the team clean-sheet chance; team xG is expected team goals. A faded crest means no minutes in GW7.

How the suggested action is chosen

The action is the first week of the transfer plan. The plan searches the next eight gameweeks for which moves to make and when: one or two a week, or a roll. Each move must clear a three-point margin on top of any four-point hit; hits are allowed only for an urgent move this week, a free transfer banked at the end is worth 1.5 points, and later weeks count for less because their projections are less certain. It keeps the squad's cheap bench slots: an enabler leaves only for another cheap player, or in a two-move restructure. This is a conservative heuristic, not a calibrated guarantee.

Bench Boost and Triple Captain are timed inside the plan when their availability is verified, against their best later week this half. Free Hit is highlighted only when its own planner has a strong next-gameweek case; Wildcard is a longer-window decision in the chip planner. Double gameweeks remain unsupported. Check your actual squad, bank and free transfers before acting.

Your moves

Who to sell, who to buy, and who takes the armband.

Transfer plan, GW8–15

Each week scores the best eleven from your fifteen, the captain twice, and the bench by its chance of coming on (all of it on Bench Boost week). A plan may roll, or make one or two moves a week. A hit costs 4 and is taken only this week, only when urgent: a starter ruled out, or a signing top five in his position on xGI per 90 with a fair next fixture. Every move must also clear a 3-point margin, and a free transfer still banked at the end is worth 1.5. A chip is played only when its week beats waiting by 2 points, and an enabler is swapped for another bench player only ahead of a planned Bench Boost. Beyond next week's predicted line-up, a player's chance of starting follows his last three matches, drifting a quarter of the way back toward his season-long rate each week. Later weeks count for less, because their projections are less certain. Uses the transfer model's projections and current prices; the first week's captain follows the captaincy card.

Across GW8–15 these moves project 546 points, +28.7 against making no transfers, after hits. Re-planned at every update, so later weeks are a default, not a commitment.

Cheap slots kept: Diop (DEF 3.9m), Dubravka (GKP 4.0m), Hughes (MID 4.3m). One leaves only for another cheap player (up to 4.5m keepers and defenders, 5.0m midfielders and forwards), or in a two-move restructure where a cheap player arrives in another position the same week.

Captaincy decision matrix

This gameweek's top armband candidates from your XI, overlaid across five axes. Each axis is scaled to that metric's own real range (0.5x-2.0x for the fixture multiplier, 0-100% for start certainty, and so on - see captaincy.py) - not to whoever else is shown - so the edge of the chart means the same thing every week: genuinely one of the best fixtures or returns anyone gets, not just the best of this shortlist. Two candidates from the same club can also share an axis exactly (same team, same fixture), which is a genuine tie, not missing data. Price watch

Both figures are progress towards a price change, which fires at 100%: the big number is where he is now, the small one is where FPL forecast him in two days. Net transfers are raw, so a widely-owned player needs far more of them to move the same distance.A change fires at 100%. Prices update once a day, so this is only worth anything before it happens. Progress is relative to a player's own ownership, which is why a small net-transfer figure can sit above a large one.
